title: AI-tools training → productivity
teaser: Weak performers nudged in; tool use is the middle step; kudos is a collider.
question: Did the AI-tools training raise productivity, and by how much?
ask: Leadership wants the average lift in this quarter's output score.

outcome.name: out_m
outcome.meaning: output score this quarter (the productivity measure)

variables.name: q_score
variables.meaning: output score for the previous quarter (same scale)

instrument.name: slot_open
instrument.meaning: 1 = a course seat was open in the employee's time zone (seats were allocated by random draw)

mediator.name: usage_idx
mediator.meaning: how much the employee used AI tools, from tool logs
mediator.recorded: during the quarter, after the course

post_treatment.name: kudos
post_treatment.meaning: recognition points from peers and managers

notes.text: Taking the course was voluntary. Managers nudged people who had a weak previous quarter to take it.
Recognition points are partly given for good output and partly for completing training.
Managers also hand-picked people they saw as high-potential for the first seats, based on their own impressions; that list wasn't kept.

traps.name: Weak performers nudged in
traps.text: Reverse causation: leaving out last quarter's score understates the effect.

traps.name: Middle step with a misleading name
traps.text: usage_idx is how the course works; controlling for it hides most of the effect.

traps.name: Collider
traps.text: kudos is caused by both training and output.

traps.name: Unrecorded manager picks
traps.text: Hand-picked high-potential staff took the course and improve anyway; with no seat draw recorded, not answerable.

hidden.name: U_ambition
hidden.label: which people managers privately saw as high-potential
